Syed Mahabubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner 
Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate, Instructed by Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ----- For Respondent

Phul Chandra Mia being dead his heirs: Nawban Chandra and another ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
3. Respondent No. 6 Eastern Bank Limited being plaintiff instituted Dewani Mokaddama No. 51 of 1998 (Title Suit No. 51 of 1998) before the then Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka (hereinafter referred to as the Adalat) for recovery of loan amounting to Tk. 1,11,59,799.20 impleading Minar International (a sole proprietorship business of J.H. Gazi), Md. Phul Chand Mia and others as defendants of the suit. Defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3 made their appearance in the suit and filed two sets of written statements denying the material allegations made by the plaintiff in the plaint. In both the written statements it was stated that the suit suffers from defect of parties; as such it is not maintainable. Even defendant No. 4 died long before of institution of the suit where his heirs have not been made defendants by way of substitution. The learned Judge of the Adalat, without considering this fact, passed the decree on 10.04.2001 against a dead person which is a nullity. 

 4. However, when judgment-debtors failed to pay the decretal amount the plaintiff-decree-holder Bank filed Artha Jari Case No. 97 of 2002 before the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 3, Dhaka on 5.8.2002 for realization of decretal amount. In the execution case several attempts were made to sell the mortgaged property in auction by publishing notice in the daily news papers but of no result. Ultimately on the basis of the application filed by the decree-holder, Bank a certificate was issued under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 vesting the title of the suit property in favour of the Bank on 13.3.2003. Thereafter, plaintiff decree-holder published a notice in the daily newspaper inviting tender for auction sale of the mortgaged property belonging to defendant No. 4; the judgment-debtor. Thereafter the heirs of the defendant No. 4 filed this writ petition challenging the legality of the impugned decree under execution since judgment-debtor, defendant No. 4 died long before filing of the suit. 

 5. On the other hand, respondent No. 6, the Bank, the decree-holder filed an affidavit-in-opposition contending inter-alia, that order contesting defendants of the suit raised the question of maintainability of the suit on the ground that respondent No. 4 died and his heirs have not been made parties. Ultimately the executing court has rejected such proposition of the judgment-debtor with reference to Order XXII, Rule 4(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure since defendant No. 4 died during the pendency of the suit where he was not contesting.
